tips: Sichuan hotpot is a staple, but be prepared for the intense numbing heat of the Sichuan peppercorn (málà)
The local lifestyle is famously slow and relaxed compared to the hustle of Beijing or Shanghai
Spend an afternoon drinking jasmine tea and playing Mahjong in People's Park
Book tickets to the Giant Panda Breeding Base in advance and arrive early to see them active
WeChat Pay and Alipay are absolutely mandatory for payments; cash is rarely accepted

geography: Located in the rolling plains of North Texas along the Trinity River
Part of a massive, heavily urbanized region known as the Dallas-Fort Worth (DFW) Metroplex
Humid subtropical climate — blisteringly hot summers and mild winters with occasional ice storms
history: 1841: Founded as a trading post by John Neely Bryan
1870s: The arrival of multiple railroad lines turns it into a major business center
1930s: The East Texas oil boom floods the city with massive wealth and corporate headquarters
1963: President John F. Kennedy is assassinated in Dealey Plaza
Late 20th century: Rapid expansion as a global center for telecommunications and aviation
transportation: DFW International Airport is a massive global hub; Dallas Love Field (DAL) handles regional flights
DART operates the longest light rail system in the United States, plus extensive buses
An intensely car-centric culture reliant on massive multi-lane highways and tollways
Ride-sharing is widely used, though distances can make fares expensive
Walkability is largely restricted to specific neighborhoods like Uptown or Deep Ellum
tips: A rental car is virtually essential to navigate the vast distances of the Metroplex
Summer heat is oppressive; limit outdoor activities to the early morning and rely on air conditioning
Tex-Mex and smoked BBQ brisket are the undisputed kings of the local culinary scene
Visit the Sixth Floor Museum at Dealey Plaza for a sobering look at JFK's life and assassination
If driving, get a TollTag or be prepared for mail-in bills, as many major highways are tolled

geography: Located on the central-east coast of the Qatar Peninsula on the Persian Gulf
Completely flat, arid desert terrain reclaimed heavily from the sea
Hot desert climate — extraordinarily hot and humid summers, with pleasant, mild winters
history: 1820s: Founded as a pearling and fishing offshoot of the town of Al Bidda
1916: Becomes a British protectorate
1971: Declared the capital following Qatar's independence from Britain
1990s: Exploitation of massive offshore natural gas reserves triggers hyper-rapid modernization
2022: Hosted the FIFA World Cup, spurring a complete overhaul of national infrastructure
transportation: Hamad International Airport (DOH) is a premier global transit hub
The newly built Doha Metro is driverless, luxurious, incredibly cheap, and spotless
Karwa taxis and ride-hailing apps like Uber are abundant and heavily relied upon
The city is designed around the automobile with massive, multi-lane highways
Lusail Tram connects the northern developments to the main metro grid
tips: Dress modestly in public spaces like malls and markets (cover shoulders and knees)
Alcohol is strictly regulated and only available in licensed international hotels and clubs
Summertime heat is dangerous; locals spend the day indoors and socialize late at night
Visit Souq Waqif in the evening for an authentic experience of local food, shisha, and shopping
The weekends are Friday and Saturday; Friday mornings are very quiet due to prayers

geography: Located on the River Elbe in northern Germany
Flat coastal terrain with a vast network of canals and bridges
Temperate oceanic climate — mild summers and cool, breezy winters
history: 1189: Granted status as a Free Imperial City by Frederick I
14th century: Becomes a leading member of the Hanseatic League
1842: The Great Fire of Hamburg destroys a quarter of the inner city
1943: Suffers devastating Allied bombing (Operation Gomorrah) during WWII
Post-WWII: Rebuilds to become Europe's third-largest port and a major media hub
transportation: Hamburg Airport (HAM) serves as a major international gateway
U-Bahn and S-Bahn networks provide comprehensive city coverage
Extensive HVV bus network and iconic harbor ferries (Landungsbrücken)
StadtRAD public bike-sharing system is widely used
Hauptbahnhof is one of the busiest railway stations in Germany
tips: Take ferry line 62 for a cheap and scenic tour of the massive harbor
Visit the historic Speicherstadt, the world's largest warehouse district
The Reeperbahn in St Pauli is the center of nightlife, but stay aware of your surroundings
Carry an umbrella as the weather (Schietwetter) can be notoriously rainy and unpredictable
Eat a traditional Fischbrötchen (fish sandwich) at the Sunday morning Altona Fish Market

geography: Located in eastern China at the southern terminus of the Grand Canal
Centered around the scenic West Lake and surrounded by lush green hills
Humid subtropical climate — hot, humid summers and cool, dry winters
history: 21st century BC: Legendary founding during the Xia dynasty
1132: Becomes the capital of the Southern Song dynasty, flourishing as a global metropolis
13th century: Marco Polo describes it as the most beautiful and magnificent city in the world
2016: Hosted the G20 summit, boosting its international profile
2023: Hosted the Asian Games, driving massive infrastructure upgrades
transportation: Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport (HGH)
Rapidly expanding Hangzhou Metro system with over a dozen lines
Major high-speed rail hub connecting to Shanghai in under an hour
Extensive public bus network and massive shared bicycle infrastructure
Electric vehicles heavily dominate the local taxi and ride-hailing fleets
tips: Alipay is absolutely essential, as Hangzhou is the headquarters of Alibaba and is virtually cashless
Visit a traditional teahouse near West Lake to taste the famous Longjing (Dragon Well) green tea
Rent a shared bicycle to explore the vast and scenic perimeter of West Lake
Weekends at West Lake are extremely crowded; try visiting early in the morning
The high-speed train to Shanghai is incredibly convenient but book tickets in advance during holidays

geography: Located in southeastern Vietnam near the Mekong River Delta
Flat, low-lying terrain interlaced with a network of rivers and canals
Tropical savanna climate — hot year-round with a distinct wet and dry season
history: 17th century: Settled by Vietnamese moving south, displacing the Khmer
1859: Conquered by the French, who name it Saigon and leave a lasting architectural legacy
1955–1975: Serves as the capital of the Republic of Vietnam (South Vietnam)
1975: The Fall of Saigon marks the end of the Vietnam War
1976: Officially renamed Ho Chi Minh City, though 'Saigon' remains widely used
transportation: Tan Son Nhat International Airport (SGN) is located heavily within the urban center
An urban metro network is currently under construction and heavily delayed
Motorbikes are the undisputed kings of the road, numbering in the millions
Ride-hailing apps like Grab (offering both cars and motorbike taxis) are essential
Public buses exist but are difficult for non-Vietnamese speakers to navigate efficiently
tips: When crossing the street, walk slowly and predictably; motorbikes will flow around you
Download Grab for safe, cheap, and meter-free rides around the city
Vietnamese iced coffee (Cà phê sữa đá) is incredibly strong and sweet — a must-try
Be highly vigilant against bag-snatching by passing motorbikes, especially in District 1
Street food is generally safe and delicious; look for stalls with high turnover of locals

geography: Located on the central western coast of Peru along the Pacific Ocean
Built on a desert strip bounded by the Andes mountains and the sea
Mild desert climate — high humidity and persistent overcast skies (la garúa) but almost no rain
history: 1535: Founded by Spanish conquistador Francisco Pizarro as the 'City of Kings'
16th–18th centuries: Capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru, the most important city in Spanish South America
1746: Nearly destroyed by a massive earthquake and subsequent tsunami
1821: José de San Martín declares the independence of Peru in Lima
Late 20th century: Massive rural-to-urban migration leads to explosive, informal city growth
transportation: Jorge Chávez International Airport (LIM)
El Metropolitano is a heavily used Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system with dedicated lanes
Lima Metro currently has one operational elevated line, with more underground lines in development
Informal microbuses (combis and custers) are ubiquitous but chaotic and confusing for tourists
Uber and Cabify are the safest ways to travel point-to-point, especially at night
tips: Lima is one of the world's culinary capitals; eating ceviche here is a mandatory experience
Do not drink the tap water; stick exclusively to bottled or boiled water
Traffic is notoriously aggressive and gridlocked, so always build buffer time into your plans
Stick to safer tourist districts like Miraflores and Barranco, especially after dark
The sky is famously grey for half the year, but the sunsets over the Pacific in summer are spectacular

geography: Located on the Atlantic coast of southeastern Florida
Flat, low-lying coastal terrain extremely vulnerable to sea-level rise
Tropical monsoon climate — hot, humid summers with daily thunderstorms and warm, dry winters
history: 1896: Incorporated as a city, spurred by the arrival of Henry Flagler's railway
1920s: The Florida land boom triggers rapid population and architectural growth
1959: The Cuban Revolution prompts a massive influx of Cuban exiles, permanently altering the city's culture
1980s: The 'Cocaine Cowboys' era brings high crime and intense federal scrutiny
Today: A major international hub for finance, culture, and Latin American trade
transportation: Miami International Airport (MIA)
Metrorail (elevated rapid transit) and Metromover (free downtown people mover)
Metrobus network covering the wider Miami-Dade county
Highly car-centric city where renting a car or using Uber/Lyft is often necessary
Brightline high-speed rail connects Miami to Orlando and other Florida cities
tips: Spanish is spoken just as much, if not more, than English in many parts of the city
Sunscreen and mosquito repellent are absolute necessities year-round
Explore Little Havana for authentic Cuban coffee (cafecito), cigars, and domino games
Hurricane season runs from June to November; keep an eye on weather forecasts
South Beach is famous for its Art Deco architecture and nightlife, but food and drinks there are heavily overpriced

geography: Located on the Island of Montreal at the confluence of the Saint Lawrence and Ottawa rivers
Centered around Mount Royal, a three-peaked hill in the heart of the city
Humid continental climate — warm, humid summers and severely cold, snowy winters
history: 1642: Founded as the French missionary settlement of Ville-Marie
1760: Surrendered to British forces during the Seven Years' War
1832: Incorporated as a city, eventually becoming the economic capital of Canada until the 1970s
1967: Hosted the highly successful Expo 67
1976: Hosted the Summer Olympic Games
transportation: Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (YUL)
The STM Metro is entirely underground, featuring unique rubber-tired trains and striking station art
Extensive bus network integrated with the metro system
BIXI public bike-sharing system is highly popular during the warmer months
The Underground City (RÉSO) provides kilometers of heated pedestrian tunnels to escape the winter cold
tips: French is the official language; greeting people with a simple 'Bonjour' is polite before switching to English
Poutine and Montreal-style smoked meat sandwiches are essential culinary experiences
Winter is bitterly cold; utilize the massive Underground City to stay warm while shopping and commuting
Buy an OPUS card for easy access to the metro and bus network
During summer, the city comes alive with massive street fairs and the International Jazz Festival

geography: Located in the center of the Bohemian Basin in the Czech Republic
Bisected by the Vltava River and characterized by hilly terrain
Humid continental climate — warm, pleasant summers and chilly, snowy winters
history: 9th century: Founded with the establishment of Prague Castle
14th century: Flourishes as the capital of the Holy Roman Empire under Charles IV
1618: The Defenestration of Prague triggers the devastating Thirty Years' War
1989: The Velvet Revolution peacefully ends decades of communist rule
1992: The historic city center is designated a UNESCO World Heritage site
transportation: Václav Havel Airport Prague (PRG)
Highly efficient public transit consisting of three metro lines (A, B, C)
Dense and iconic red tram network serving the entire city center and suburbs
Extensive bus routes connecting areas not served by rail
Highly walkable historic center with many pedestrian-only cobblestone zones
tips: Validate your transit ticket in the yellow machines before your first ride, or face steep fines
Czech beer (Pilsner) is world-famous and often cheaper than bottled water in restaurants
Avoid exchanging money at street kiosks in the tourist center to avoid terrible exchange rates; use ATMs
The Astronomical Clock chimes every hour, but beware of pickpockets in the gathered crowd
Wear comfortable, flat shoes; the beautiful cobblestone streets will destroy high heels

geography: Located in the central-western portion of the Italian Peninsula on the Tiber River
Historically built on seven hills
Mediterranean climate — hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters
history: 753 BC: Legendary founding by Romulus and Remus
1st century AD: Becomes the center of the vast Roman Empire
15th–16th centuries: Replaces Florence as the center of the Italian Renaissance
1871: Becomes the capital of the newly unified Kingdom of Italy
1929: The Lateran Treaty establishes Vatican City as an independent microstate within Rome
transportation: Leonardo da Vinci–Fiumicino (FCO) and Ciampino (CIA) international airports
Metropolitana di Roma has three lines (A, B, C), limited in scope due to constant archaeological discoveries
Extensive but frequently delayed bus and tram networks operated by ATAC
Termini Station serves as the massive central hub for regional and high-speed rail
Cobblestone streets and heavy traffic make driving and cycling challenging
tips: Book tickets for the Colosseum and Vatican Museums months in advance to avoid hours-long lines
Never order a cappuccino after 11 AM; Italians consider it strictly a morning breakfast drink
Carry a reusable water bottle to fill up at the thousands of free public fountains (nasoni) scattered around the city
Dinner starts late, usually around 8:30 PM, and tipping is generally not expected or required
Beware of aggressive ticket touts and pickpockets around major tourist sites and Termini station

geography: Located in northern China along the coast of the Bohai Sea
Flat coastal plain traversed by the Hai River
Humid continental climate — hot, humid summers and cold, very dry winters
history: 1404: Officially named Tianjin ('Heavenly Ford') and fortified as a military post
1860: Opened to foreign trade following the Second Opium War, leading to the creation of foreign concessions
1900: Heavily involved in the Boxer Rebellion and subsequently occupied by the Eight-Nation Alliance
1949: Becomes a municipality directly under the central government of the PRC
21st century: Develops the Binhai New Area to become a massive financial and logistics hub
transportation: Tianjin Binhai International Airport (TSN)
High-speed rail connects Tianjin to Beijing in roughly 30 minutes
Rapidly expanding Tianjin Metro system
Extensive bus network and widely available shared bicycles
Major international cruise port and cargo shipping hub
tips: Take the 30-minute high-speed train from Beijing for an easy and fascinating day trip
Visit the Five Great Avenues (Wudadao) to see beautifully preserved European concession architecture
Try Goubuli baozi (steamed stuffed buns) and Jianbing guozi (savory crepes), the city's famous street foods
Tianjin is famous in China for its comedic 'Xiangsheng' (cross talk) culture, reflecting the locals' relaxed humor
As with all of China, Alipay or WeChat Pay is required for nearly all transactions

geography: Located on a T-shaped island jutting into the Persian Gulf
Surrounded by flat, barren desert and coastal mangroves
Hot desert climate — blistering, intensely humid summers and highly pleasant, mild winters
history: 1761: Settled by the Bani Yas tribe after the discovery of fresh water
1958: Discovery of massive oil reserves transforms the impoverished pearling village into a wealthy metropolis
1971: Becomes the capital of the newly formed United Arab Emirates under Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan
21st century: Massive diversification efforts into tourism, culture (Louvre Abu Dhabi), and renewable energy (Masdar City)
transportation: Zayed International Airport (AUH) is the home of Etihad Airways
Highly car-centric infrastructure with wide, multi-lane highways
Public bus network operated by the Department of Transport (DoT)
Taxis are plentiful, relatively cheap, and heavily regulated; ride-hailing apps like Uber and Careem are also common
Currently lacks a metro system, though plans have been discussed for years
tips: Strict modest dress codes apply when visiting the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque; women must cover their hair and bodies fully
Summers are too hot for outdoor activities; plan your trip between November and March
Alcohol is restricted to licensed hotels, bars, and clubs; public intoxication is strictly prohibited
Rent a car or rely heavily on taxis/Careem, as walking is largely impractical due to heat and urban layout
The city is generally quieter and more family-oriented than neighboring Dubai

geography: Located on the Brisbane River in Queensland
Built on low-lying floodplains between Moreton Bay and the Great Dividing Range
Humid subtropical climate — warm, wet summers and mild, dry winters
history: 1824: Established as a penal settlement for secondary offenders from Sydney
1859: Becomes the capital of the newly separated colony of Queensland
1988: Hosted the World Expo, sparking significant urban development
2011 & 2022: Experienced devastating and widespread river flooding
2032: Scheduled to host the Summer Olympic and Paralympic Games
transportation: Brisbane Airport (BNE)
Extensive busway network with dedicated lanes separated from regular traffic
Queensland Rail commuter train network connecting to the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast
CityCat ferries provide scenic and practical transit along the winding river
Cross River Rail project is currently under construction to expand subway capacity
tips: Get a Translink Go Card for all public transport including the CityCat ferries
Take advantage of the free CityHopper ferry that loops around the inner city
Visit South Bank for its man-made beach and extensive parklands
Sun protection is absolutely critical year-round due to the intense Australian sun
Be aware of swooping magpies during the spring breeding season

geography: Located in northern Egypt along the banks of the Nile River
Sprawls across the Nile Delta and borders the arid Sahara Desert
